clue.text: Poor man with urge to enter the legal profession

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the word for the legal profession

parts.note: barristers collectively are called the Bar
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A struggling man is pushed to train as a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is a pauper who asks strangers for money, the very type of a poor man.

clue.text: Channel Island glass losing money? Just the opposite making a profit.

indicators.note: just the opposite means the whole assembled string is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for Channel Islands

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the eyeglass

parts.note: a monocle is a single eyeglass
L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Guernsey optician's lens costing money, then turning a profit instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing money' removes L from MONOCLE, giving MONOCE; CI plus MONOCE is then turned round by 'Just the opposite'.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic venture is one that pays its way or yields a return.

clue.text: Stick to the point at issue, showing sense

parts.note: gum is a sticky substance and to gum is to stick

indicators.note: at issue suggests the letters of point are in dispute and reordered

explanation.surface: Keeping to the matter under debate shows good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is practical common sense and resourcefulness.

clue.text: Campanologist can sound familiar

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer is able to make a well-known noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer's skill is to peal a bell; the idiom means to seem recognisable.

clue.text: Tart instruction to printers- "Put back in"

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the printers' instruction

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to let the original stand
the rump is the back end or hindquarters

explanation.surface: A sharp note to the typesetters demands that a deleted passage be restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' looks like the printers' instruction itself; in fact 'back' is RUMP, put inside STET, and 'Put' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart is a slang word for a woman of loose morals, an old meaning of strumpet.

clue.text: Procrustes might go for a walk

explanation.surface: The mythical villain might take a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Procrustes, in Greek myth, stretched his guests to fit his bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Procrustes racked victims' limbs longer; the idiom means taking exercise on foot.

clue.text: Prudes upset after you, so to speak, took over

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the sound of you
so to speak signals that the word you is replaced by the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U

indicators.note: upset means the letters of prudes are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Prim people are offended once you have spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize power or a position wrongfully, taking it over.

clue.text: Prime Minister North in one beggarly pay award

parts.note: Pitt the Younger and the Elder were British prime ministers

indicators.note: in means the compass letter goes inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister and Lord North in a meagre pay settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was also a Prime Minister, which makes 'North' look like a second politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small, inadequate allowance of money.

clue.text: Axeman, one who wants to fight

parts.note: Tom is a man's name and a tomcat is a male
a means one
a hawk is a warmonger, a person favouring military action

explanation.surface: A man with an axe, someone spoiling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used by Native North Americans.

clue.text: More plebeian chap with no scholarship

explanation.surface: A working-class man who never won a college award.
explanation.definitionFit: Commoner is the comparative of common, meaning vulgar; at Oxford a commoner is an undergraduate holding no scholarship.

clue.text: Out of focus, to minimise use

indicators.note: out of means the letters are taken straight from the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Advice to blur an image so that it gets less exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom means habitual practice, the same as use in the sense of usage.

clue.text: Shorten the game

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut a match short.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to make smaller; contract is also the usual form of the card game bridge.

clue.text: Cut about a page in prominent news display

indicators.note: about means the word for cut goes around the other piece

parts.note: to slash is to cut with a sweeping stroke
p is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Trimming a page to fit a big headline story.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper splash is a front-page story given dramatic, eye-catching layout.

clue.text: The cost of such a smash in court

explanation.surface: Asking the price of a powerful tennis shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead means a running business expense; in tennis an overhead is a smash hit from above the head.

clue.text: Games that slice can ruin

indicators.note: can ruin suggests the letters of that slice are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: In golf or tennis, a sliced shot can spoil a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics are track and field sports, often called games, as in the Commonwealth Games.

clue.text: At first sight, she may overlook …

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: may and can both express permission or possibility

explanation.surface: A woman glancing at something might miss it on first viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next across clue. 'At first' takes the opening letter of 'sight'; 'she' merely joins it to CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook can mean to look over or survey, which is what a quick scan does.

clue.text: Put up with Irishman and resist change

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock Irishman

explanation.surface: Tolerating an Irish fellow and refusing to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand pat is to stick to one's position and refuse to alter it.

clue.text: Moved camp

explanation.surface: Touched by something theatrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected means emotionally stirred, and also pretentious or mannered, as camp behaviour is.

clue.text: … dress and four suits

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: she may overlook her outfit and a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn or dress up; a deck of cards contains four suits.

clue.text: Doctor previously lost heart, becoming more gloomy

indicators.note: lost heart means the central letter of the word for previously is removed

parts.note: earlier means at a previous time

explanation.surface: A physician became disheartened and sadder than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost heart' removes the middle letter L from EARLIER, leaving EARIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearier is the comparative of dreary, meaning dismal or depressing.

clue.text: Scratch about shortly to find ecclesiastical authority

indicators.note: about means the word for scratch goes round the other piece

parts.note: to claw is to scratch
anon is an old word meaning soon or shortly

explanation.surface: Scraping around briefly in search of church rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Canon law is the body of rules governing a Christian church.

clue.text: I left hospital with woman, one given to embracing

indicators.note: left means a letter has departed from the word for hospital

parts.note: a clinic is a place for medical treatment
her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A patient discharges themselves and leaves with a female companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' asks for the letter I to be removed from CLINIC, leaving CLINC.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch is to hold in a tight grip, as boxers do, so a clincher is one who embraces.

clue.text: Military man, a general, has name for girl

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: An officer and a general have a name for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleen is the Irish word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Nag to the fore in-nearly every event didn't look exceptional

indicators.note: to the fore in tells us to take the front letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A racehorse led in almost every race but looked quite ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like the horse of the surface; it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to keep irritating or pestering them, exactly as nagging does.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker who was made by another's misfortune

definitions.text: who was made by another's misfortune

explanation.surface: A furniture maker owes his success to someone else's bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SHE RAT ON, the name describes an informer who profits by betraying another person.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer; a woman who informed on someone gains through their downfall.

clue.text: Tinker -a craftsman?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a travelling mender counts as an artisan.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to tinker idly; a potter is a craftsman working in clay.

clue.text: Marriageable foreign female accepts' one rock.

indicators.note: accepts means the French word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: elle is French for she
one is the Roman numeral I
the Rock is Gibraltar, shortened to Gib

explanation.surface: A suitable foreign woman takes a single gemstone engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Eligible describes someone regarded as a desirable match for a spouse.

clue.text: Insisted on changing the order

indicators.note: on changing tells us the letters of the word insisted are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone demanded the sequence be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like part of the surface's sequence; it is the definition, and 'the' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Order in the sense of neatness or good arrangement is a synonym for tidiness.

clue.text: Clever little animal died

parts.note: a shrew is a tiny insect-eating mammal
d is the abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: A bright small creature has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute, sharp-witted and clever in judgement.
